variable {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I ∞ M]

def cotangentToCLM {x : M} (α : Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) :
    TangentSpace I x →L[Real] Real where
  toFun X := α (fun _ => X)
  map_add' X Y := by
    have h := α.toMultilinearMap.map_update_add (fun _ => 0) 0 X Y
    change α.toMultilinearMap (fun _ => X + Y) =
      α.toMultilinearMap (fun _ => X) + α.toMultilinearMap (fun _ => Y)
    rw [show (fun _ : Fin 1 => X + Y) = Function.update (fun _ => 0) 0 (X + Y) by
      funext i; fin_cases i; simp]
    rw [show (fun _ : Fin 1 => X) = Function.update (fun _ => 0) 0 X by
      funext i; fin_cases i; simp]
    rw [show (fun _ : Fin 1 => Y) = Function.update (fun _ => 0) 0 Y by
      funext i; fin_cases i; simp]
    exact h
  map_smul' c X := by
    have h := α.toMultilinearMap.map_update_smul (fun _ => 0) 0 c X
    change α.toMultilinearMap (fun _ => c • X) = c • α.toMultilinearMap (fun _ => X)
    rw [show (fun _ : Fin 1 => c • X) = Function.update (fun _ => 0) 0 (c • X) by
      funext i; fin_cases i; simp]
    rw [show (fun _ : Fin 1 => X) = Function.update (fun _ => 0) 0 X by
      funext i; fin_cases i; simp]
    exact h
  cont := α.cont.comp (continuous_pi fun _ => continuous_id)

def cotangentToDual {x : M} (α : Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) :
    Module.Dual Real (TangentSpace I x) :=
  (cotangentToCLM (I := I) α).toLinearMap

omit [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] in
@[simp] theorem cotangentToDual_apply {x : M}
    (α : Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) (X : TangentSpace I x) :
    cotangentToDual (I := I) α X = α (fun _ : Fin 1 => X) := by
  rfl

def cotangentToDualLinear {x : M} :
    Tensor0SSpace 1 I x →ₗ[Real] Module.Dual Real (TangentSpace I x) where
  toFun := cotangentToDual (I := I)
  map_add' α β := by
    ext X
    rfl
  map_smul' c α := by
    ext X
    rfl

omit [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] in
theorem cotangentToDualLinear_injective {x : M} :
    Function.Injective (cotangentToDualLinear (I := I) (x := x)) := by
  intro α β h
  ext v
  have hv :
      (fun _ : Fin 1 => v 0) = v := by
    funext i
    fin_cases i
    rfl
  have h0 := congrArg (fun L : Module.Dual Real (TangentSpace I x) => L (v 0)) h
  simpa [cotangentToDualLinear, cotangentToDual_apply, hv] using h0

def cotangentSharpLinear (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    Tensor0SSpace 1 I x →ₗ[Real] TangentSpace I x :=
  ((tangentMetricData (I := I) g x).metric.sharp).toLinearMap.comp
    (cotangentToDualLinear (I := I) (x := x))

def cotangentSharp (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M)
    (α : Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) : TangentSpace I x :=
  cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α

@[simp] theorem cotangentSharpLinear_apply
    (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) (α : Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) :
    cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α = cotangentSharp (I := I) g x α := by
  rfl

theorem cotangentSharpLinear_injective
    (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    Function.Injective (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x) := by
  intro α β h
  apply cotangentToDualLinear_injective (I := I) (x := x)
  exact ((tangentMetricData (I := I) g x).metric.sharp.injective h)

def cotangentInner (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M)
    (α β : Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) : Real :=
  g.inner x
    (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α)
    (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x β)

def cotangentFlatLinear (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    Tensor0SSpace 1 I x →ₗ[Real] Module.Dual Real (Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) where
  toFun α :=
    { toFun := fun β => cotangentInner (I := I) g x α β
      map_add' := by
        intro β γ
        let S := cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x
        have hS : S (β + γ) = S β + S γ := map_add S β γ
        change g.inner x (S α) (S (β + γ)) =
          g.inner x (S α) (S β) + g.inner x (S α) (S γ)
        rw [hS]
        simp
      map_smul' := by
        intro c β
        let S := cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x
        have hS : S (c • β) = c • S β := map_smul S c β
        change g.inner x (S α) (S (c • β)) = c * g.inner x (S α) (S β)
        rw [hS]
        simp }
  map_add' α β := by
    ext γ
    let S := cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x
    have hS : S (α + β) = S α + S β := map_add S α β
    change g.inner x (S (α + β)) (S γ) =
      g.inner x (S α) (S γ) + g.inner x (S β) (S γ)
    rw [hS]
    simp
  map_smul' c α := by
    ext β
    let S := cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x
    have hS : S (c • α) = c • S α := map_smul S c α
    change g.inner x (S (c • α)) (S β) = c * g.inner x (S α) (S β)
    rw [hS]
    simp

theorem cotangentFlatLinear_injective
    (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    Function.Injective (cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x) := by
  intro α β h
  have hsub : cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β) = 0 := by
    by_contra hsharp
    have hpos :
        0 <
          g.inner x
            (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β))
            (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β)) :=
      g.pos x (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β)) hsharp
    have h_eval :
        cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x α (α - β) =
          cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x β (α - β) :=
      congrArg
        (fun L : Module.Dual Real (Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) => L (α - β)) h
    have hdiff : cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x (α - β) (α - β) = 0 := by
      calc
        cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x (α - β) (α - β)
            = (cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x α -
                cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x β) (α - β) := by
                exact congrArg
                  (fun L : Module.Dual Real (Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) => L (α - β))
                  (map_sub (cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x) α β)
        _ = cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x α (α - β) -
              cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x β (α - β) := rfl
        _ = 0 := sub_eq_zero.mpr h_eval
    have hzero :
        g.inner x
            (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β))
            (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β)) = 0 := by
      simpa [cotangentFlatLinear, cotangentInner] using hdiff
    exact (lt_irrefl (0 : Real)) (hzero ▸ hpos)
  apply cotangentSharpLinear_injective (I := I) g x
  have hdiff :
      cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α -
        cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x β = 0 := by
    have hmap :
        cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x (α - β) =
          cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α -
            cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x β :=
      map_sub (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x) α β
    rwa [hmap] at hsub
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp hdiff

def cotangentMetricData (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    MetricFiberData (Tensor0SSpace 1 I x) :=
  MetricFiberData.ofFlat
    (cotangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x)
    (cotangentFlatLinear_injective (I := I) g x)
    (by
      intro α β
      change g.inner x
          (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α)
          (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x β) =
        g.inner x
          (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x β)
          (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α)
      exact g.symm x _ _)
    (by
      intro α
      by_cases hα : cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α = 0
      · change 0 <=
          g.inner x
            (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α)
            (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α)
        rw [hα]
        simp
      · exact le_of_lt (g.pos x (cotangentSharpLinear (I := I) g x α) hα))

end

import Definitions.Def_OpenGA_WidthComparisonData
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
set_option autoImplicit false
open Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace OpenGA

/-- Analytic input before integrating the short-time area estimate. The same
time interval and sequence cutoff work for every slice. The derivative bound
allows slices below the initial supremum to use their initial area gap;
it does not demand negative area derivative from constant endpoint slices. -/
structure WidthAreaEvolutionData (width : ℝ → ℝ) (time scalar : ℝ) where
  realizer : FiniteEnergyPair
  realizer_conformal : realizer.IsConformal
  realized_energy : realizer.energy = width time
  competitor : ℕ → Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → FiniteEnergyPair
  energy_cap : ℕ → ℝ
  energy_le_cap : ∀ j p, (competitor j p).energy ≤ energy_cap j
  cap_tendsto : Tendsto energy_cap atTop (𝓝 (width time))
  area : ℕ → Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ → ℝ
  area_initial : ∀ j p, area j p time = (competitor j p).area
  uniform_evolution : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∃ start : ℕ,
    ∀ j ≥ start,
      (∀ s ∈ Ioo time (time + δ), width s ≤ ⨆ p, area j p s) ∧
      (∀ p, ContinuousOn (area j p) (Icc time (time + δ))) ∧
      (∀ p s, s ∈ Ioo time (time + δ) → DifferentiableAt ℝ (area j p) s) ∧
      (∀ p s, s ∈ Ioo time (time + δ) →
        deriv (area j p) s ≤ -(4 * Real.pi) - scalar / 2 * realizer.area + ε +
          ((⨆ q, (competitor j q).area) - (competitor j p).area) / δ)


end OpenGA
e3bc03e8-d36a-4cb4-8941-cad17fa54760.natural_language_statement: Finite-energy comparison fields, a conformal limiting realizer, and time-dependent real area profiles. The energy caps converge to the initial width. For every positive error, one time interval and one sequence cutoff work for every slice: the evolved family bounds the width and each area derivative is at most $-4π-R A_*/2+ε+(A_j-A_{j,p})/δ$, where $A_j$ is the initial slice supremum. The area gap allows low-area slices to have nonnegative derivative. These are analytic data; their realization by geometric sweepouts and the uniform derivative estimate are separate open obligations.

    {g_fam : ℝ → SmoothRiemannianMetric I M} {t₀ : ℝ}

            HasDerivAt
              (fun s : ℝ => chartGramMatrix (I := I) (g_fam s) x₀ x i j)
              (D t x) t) ∧
        ContinuousOn
          (fun p : ℝ × M =>
            chartGramMatrix (I := I) (g_fam p.1) x₀ p.2 i j)
          (Set.univ ×ˢ (trivializationAt E (TangentSpace I) x₀).baseSet) ∧
        ContinuousOn
          (fun p : ℝ × M => D p.1 p.2)
          (Set.univ ×ˢ (trivializationAt E (TangentSpace I) x₀).baseSet)) :
    MetricFamilyRegularAt (I := I) g_fam t₀ := by sorry

Suppose every chart Gram entry $G_{ij}(t,x)$ of a smooth metric family has a time derivative $D_{ij}(t,x)$ for every real time on its chart base, and both $G_{ij}$ and $D_{ij}$ are jointly continuous there. Then the family satisfies `MetricFamilyRegularAt` at every specified time. This packages exactly those global chart-time hypotheses; it does not assert their existence for arbitrary metric families.

theorem PoincareFormalization.persistent_comparison_data_of_not_homeomorph_sphere
    (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) M]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace M] [CompactSpace M]
    (hnot : ¬ Nonempty (M ≃ₜ ↥(Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (3 + 1))) 1))) :
    ∃ initialWidth : ℝ, 0 ≤ initialWidth ∧ ∀ finalTime : ℝ, 0 < finalTime →
      Nonempty (OpenGA.WidthComparisonTrace initialWidth finalTime) := by sorry
ed56bd90-927e-45c1-81d1-b79a2ca8a034.natural_language_statement:
Let $M$ be a compact, simply connected, Hausdorff topological three-manifold without boundary. Assume hypothetically that $M$ is not homeomorphic to the unit three-sphere. Construct a constant $W_0\ge0$ such that for every $T>0$ there is a finite width comparison trace on $[0,T]$, with initial width at most $W_0$.

A finite partition of a time interval carries continuous scalar and width profiles, normalized initial scalar bound, a common initial width bound, nonnegative widths, the scalar differential inequality, upward scalar jumps and downward width jumps. At each time before the end of a partition interval, an area-energy width comparison bundle is supplied. The width slope inequality is deliberately a conclusion of the comparison theorem, not a field of this bundle. This records analytic data to be constructed from geometry; it does not define a surgery flow.

A finite-energy pair consists of a measure space, a real inner product space, and two almost-everywhere strongly measurable fields $v,w$ with integrable energy. Write

$$A(p)=\int\sqrt{\|v\|^2\|w\|^2-\langle v,w\rangle^2},\qquad E(p)=\frac12\int(\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2).$$

Conformality means orthogonality and equal norms almost everywhere. A width comparison at time $t$, with scalar parameter $R$, supplies a conformal realizer $r$ with $E(r)=W(t)$; pairs $p_{j,u}$ for $j\in\mathbb N$, $u\in[0,1]$; caps $c_j$ with $E(p_{j,u})\le c_j$ and $c_j\to W(t)$; and, for every $\varepsilon>0$, numbers $\delta>0$ and $J$ such that for $j\ge J$ and $t<s<t+\delta$,

$$W(s)\le\sup_{u\in[0,1]}A(p_{j,u})+(s-t)\left(-4\pi-\frac R2 A(r)+\varepsilon\right).$$

The fields are analytic input data. No surface differential, sweepout homotopy class, harmonic map, or Ricci flow is defined by this bundle.

This is a composite open construction problem refining the existing persistent-profile target. Remaining geometric work includes a smooth model and normalization, the prime-factor and sweepout reductions, surgery-flow existence, scalar comparison, conformal width realizers, uniform short-time comparison estimates, endpoint continuity and surgery compatibility. In particular, this statement does not assert that these tasks are solved.

theorem OpenGA.areaDensity_eq_normDet (L : E →ₗ[ℝ] F) (b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin 2) ℝ E) :
    areaDensity (L (b 0)) (L (b 1)) = L.normDet := by sorry
eddc764e-527d-4d07-a812-94f60b637407.natural_language_statement:
Let $E$ be a two-dimensional real inner product space, let $F$ be any real inner product space, and let $L:E\to F$ be linear. For every orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2)$ of $E$,

$$\sqrt{\|Le_1\|^2\|Le_2\|^2-\langle Le_1,Le_2\rangle^2}=\operatorname{normDet}(L).$$

The right side is Mathlib's nonnegative volume factor of a linear map. No injectivity assumption is made; rank-deficient maps are included. This is a pointwise linear-algebra interface for the surface Jacobian formula, not a construction of a manifold differential or a Sobolev surface integral.

/-!
# Varifolds induced by weighted measurable maps

Push a finite weighted measure through `x ↦ (f x, P x)`, retaining both the
position and the plane. `J` is a nonnegative density; when it is the Jacobian
and `P` is the differential's image, this is the parametrized-surface construction.
The latter identification is made separately in `Varifold.Parametrization`.

The choice of plane where `J = 0` does not affect the varifold. This is the
extension-independence needed at degenerate differentials in CM Section 1.3.
Reference: Colding-Minicozzi, arXiv:0707.0108, Section 1.3, p. 5.
-/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal CompactlySupported

namespace OpenGA.Varifold

variable {X E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] {k : ℕ}










theorem testIntegral_ofWeightedMap (μ : Measure X) (f : X → E)
    (P : X → Grassmannian E k) (J : X → ℝ≥0) (hf : Measurable f) (hP : Measurable P)
    (hJ : Measurable J) (hfinite : (∫⁻ x, (J x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μ) < ∞)
    (φ : C_c(E × Grassmannian E k, ℝ)) :
    (ofWeightedMap μ f P J hf hP hfinite).testIntegral φ =
      ∫ x, (J x : ℝ) * φ (f x, P x) ∂μ := by sorry



end OpenGA.Varifold
ede9d85f-3bc2-4f0d-a18e-6644aa9e8a64.natural_language_statement:
For measurable $f:X\to E$, $P:X\to G_k(E)$ and $J:X\to[0,\infty)$ of finite integral, and every compactly supported continuous $\phi$ on positions and planes,

$$\int\phi\,d((f,P)_*(J\mu))=\int_X J(x)\phi(f(x),P(x))\,d\mu(x).$$

f1d3ae1f-1536-40e5-afeb-5a67fdbdbad8.natural_language_statement:
Let $f:N\to(M,g)$ be a smooth immersion of a finite-dimensional Hausdorff manifold, and put $h=f^*g$. Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be measurable and suppose $p:\mathbb R^2\to N$ is differentiable at every point of $A$. Then

$$\int_A J_h p(u)\,du=\int_A J_g(f\circ p)(u)\,du.$$

The integrals are Bochner integrals, so the equality also applies with Lean's total-integral convention; it identifies the ordinary finite areas whenever the density is integrable. Multiplicity is retained because neither map is required to be injective. This is compatibility of local patch integrals, not a claim about branch points or finite-time extinction.

def ofFlat
    (flat : V →ₗ[Real] Module.Dual Real V)
    (hinj : Function.Injective flat)

def inner (D : MetricFiberData V) (v w : V) : Real :=
  D.flat v w

def sharp (D : MetricFiberData V) : Module.Dual Real V ≃ₗ[Real] V :=
  D.flat.symm

@[simp] theorem inner_apply (D : MetricFiberData V) (v w : V) :
    D.inner v w = D.flat v w := by
  rfl

theorem inner_nonneg (D : MetricFiberData V) (v : V) :
    0 <= D.inner v v := by
  exact D.nonneg v

theorem inner_self_eq_zero_iff (D : MetricFiberData V) (v : V) :
    D.inner v v = 0 ↔ v = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hv
    have hvw : forall w : V, D.inner v w = 0 := by
      intro w
      by_contra hne
      let a := D.inner v w
      let b := D.inner w w
      let t := -((b + 1) / (2 * a))
      have ha : a ≠ 0 := hne
      have hquad : 0 <= D.inner (w + t • v) (w + t • v) :=
        D.inner_nonneg (w + t • v)
      have hcalc : D.inner (w + t • v) (w + t • v) = -1 := by
        have hexpand :
            D.inner (w + t • v) (w + t • v) =
              b + 2 * t * a + t * t * D.inner v v := by
          unfold inner a b
          simp only [map_add, map_smul, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply,
            smul_eq_mul]
          rw [D.symm w v]
          simp [inner]
          ring_nf
        rw [hexpand, hv]
        unfold t b a
        field_simp [ha]
        ring
      linarith
    have hflat : D.flat v = 0 := by
      ext w
      exact hvw w
    exact D.flat.injective (by simpa using hflat)
  · intro hv
    simp [hv, inner]

@[reducible] def toCore (D : MetricFiberData V) : InnerProductSpace.Core Real V where
  inner := fun v w => D.inner v w
  conj_inner_symm := by
    intro x y
    exact D.symm y x
  re_inner_nonneg := by
    intro x
    simpa using D.inner_nonneg x
  add_left := by
    intro x y z
    simp [MetricFiberData.inner, map_add]
  smul_left := by
    intro x y r
    simp [MetricFiberData.inner, smul_eq_mul]
  definite := by
    intro x hx
    exact (D.inner_self_eq_zero_iff x).1 (by simpa using hx)

    letI : InnerProductSpace.Core Real V := D.toCore
    letI : NormedAddCommGroup V := InnerProductSpace.Core.toNormedAddCommGroup
    letI : InnerProductSpace Real V :=
      @InnerProductSpace.ofCore Real V _ _ _ D.toCore.toCore
    Inner.inner Real v w = D.inner v w := by
  change D.toCore.inner v w = D.inner v w
  rfl

    (A.dualMap.comp DW.flat.toLinearMap)

theorem adjoint_inner
    (DV : MetricFiberData V) (DW : MetricFiberData W)
    (A : V →ₗ[Real] W) (y : W) (x : V) :
    DV.inner (adjoint DV DW A y) x = DW.inner y (A x) := by
  unfold inner adjoint
  change
    DV.flat (DV.flat.symm
        ((A.dualMap.comp DW.flat.toLinearMap) y)) x =

def tangentFlatLinear (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    TangentSpace I x →ₗ[Real] Module.Dual Real (TangentSpace I x) where
  toFun v := (g.inner x v).toLinearMap
  map_add' v w := by
    ext u
    change g.inner x (v + w) u = g.inner x v u + g.inner x w u
    simp
  map_smul' c v := by
    ext u
    change g.inner x (c • v) u = c • g.inner x v u
    simp

theorem tangentFlatLinear_injective
    (g : SmoothMetric I M) (x : M) :
    Function.Injective (tangentFlatLinear (I := I) g x) := by
  intro v w hvw
  have hzero : forall z : TangentSpace I x, g.inner x (v - w) z = 0 := by
    intro z
    have h := congrArg (fun L : Module.Dual Real (TangentSpace I x) => L z) hvw
    simp only [tangentFlatLinear_apply] at h
    have hsub : g.inner x (v - w) z = g.inner x v z - g.inner x w z := by
      rw [map_sub]
      rfl
    rw [hsub, sub_eq_zero]
    exact h
  by_contra hne
  have hvw_ne : v - w ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hne
  have hpos : 0 < g.inner x (v - w) (v - w) := g.pos x (v - w) hvw_ne
  exact (lt_irrefl (0 : Real)) ((hzero (v - w)) ▸ hpos)

    TangentSpace I x ≃ₗ[Real] Module.Dual Real (TangentSpace I x) :=

The metric and distance are upstream/Mathlib constructions. The ball interface

import Definitions.Def_DifferentialGeometry_RiemannianDistance

noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false

open Bundle Set DifferentialGeometry
open scoped Manifold ContDiff ENNReal

namespace Riemannian.RiemannianMetric

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H}
  {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I ∞ M]

/-- **Math.** The open ball for the distance induced by the specified metric. -/
def geodesicBall (g : RiemannianMetric I M) (p : M) (r : ℝ) : Set M :=
  {x | riemannianEDistOf (I := I) g p x < ENNReal.ofReal r}

/-- **Math.** Membership in a metric ball is the strict distance inequality. -/
@[simp] theorem mem_geodesicBall (g : RiemannianMetric I M) (p x : M) (r : ℝ) :
    x ∈ g.geodesicBall p r ↔ riemannianEDistOf (I := I) g p x < ENNReal.ofReal r :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- **Math.** A ball of nonpositive radius is empty. -/
theorem geodesicBall_eq_empty (g : RiemannianMetric I M) (p : M)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≤ 0) : g.geodesicBall p r = ∅ := by
  ext x
  simp [geodesicBall, ENNReal.ofReal_of_nonpos hr]

/-- **Math.** Increasing the radius increases the ball. -/
theorem geodesicBall_mono (g : RiemannianMetric I M) (p : M) :
    Monotone (g.geodesicBall p) := by
  intro r R hrR x hx
  exact lt_of_lt_of_le hx (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal hrR)

/-- **Math.** The center lies in precisely the positive-radius balls. -/
@[simp] theorem self_mem_geodesicBall (g : RiemannianMetric I M) (p : M) (r : ℝ) :
    p ∈ g.geodesicBall p r ↔ 0 < r := by
  simp [geodesicBall, riemannianEDistOf_self]

/-- **Math.** A positive-radius ball is nonempty. -/
theorem geodesicBall_nonempty (g : RiemannianMetric I M) (p : M)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : (g.geodesicBall p r).Nonempty :=
  ⟨p, (g.self_mem_geodesicBall p r).mpr hr⟩

end Riemannian.RiemannianMetric

Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $M$, $p\in M$ and $r\in\mathbb R$. Define

$$B_g(p,r)=\{x\in M:d_g(p,x)<\max(r,0)\}.$$

For $r>0$ this is the usual metric ball; for $r\le0$ it is empty. The bundle includes its immediate membership, radius inclusion and center-membership properties. The distance is the imported DifferentialGeometry construction. No geodesic convexity, completeness or curvature bound is assumed.

theorem tensor0SModelAt_applyInput_eq
    (r s : ℕ) {x₀ x : M}
    (hx : x ∈ (trivializationAt E (TangentSpace I) x₀).baseSet)
    (T : TensorRSSpace (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) r s x)
    (θ : Tensor0SSpace (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) r x) :

        (fun x => Tensor0SSpace s I x) x₀) ⟨x, T θ⟩).2 =
      (((trivializationAt (TensorRSModel r s 𝕜 E)
          (fun x => TensorRSSpace r s I x) x₀) ⟨x, T⟩).2)
        (((trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
          (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀) ⟨x, θ⟩).2) := by
  let := tensor0SBundleTopology (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) r
  let := tensor0SBundleTopology (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) s
  let := tensorRSBundleTopology (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) r s
  ext v
  rw [Tensor0SSpace.trivializationAt_apply (𝕜 := 𝕜) (I := I)
    (x₀ := x₀) (x := x) s]
  rw [TensorRSSpace.trivializationAt_apply (𝕜 := 𝕜) (I := I)
    (x₀ := x₀) (x := x) r s hx]
  have hθ :
      (trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
        (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀).symmL 𝕜 x
        (((trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
          (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀) ⟨x, θ⟩).2) = θ := by
    have hcoord :
        (trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
          (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀).continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜 x θ =
          ((trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
            (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀) ⟨x, θ⟩).2 := by
      rw [Bundle.Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt_apply]
      exact congrFun ((trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
        (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀).coe_linearMapAt_of_mem (R := 𝕜) hx) θ
    rw [← hcoord]
    exact (trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
      (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀).symmL_continuousLinearMapAt
        (R := 𝕜) hx θ
  rw [hθ]

    (T : (x : M) ->

    (T : TensorRSField n r s (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M))
    (θ : Tensor0SField n r (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M)) :
    Tensor0SField n s (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) := by

  letI := tensor0SBundleTopology (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H) (I := I) (M := M) s

  refine ⟨tensorRSFieldApplyInputFun (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (H := H)
    (I := I) (M := M) (r := r) (s := s) (fun x => T x) (fun x => θ x), ?_⟩
  intro x₀
  rw [contMDiffAt_section]
  have hT := T.contMDiff x₀
  rw [contMDiffAt_section] at hT
  have hθ := θ.contMDiff x₀
  rw [contMDiffAt_section] at hθ
  have hcombine :
      ContMDiffAt I 𝓘(𝕜, Tensor0SModel s 𝕜 E) n
        (fun x : M =>
          modelApplyInputBilinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) r s
            (((trivializationAt (Tensor0SModel r 𝕜 E)
                (fun x => Tensor0SSpace r I x) x₀) ⟨x, θ x⟩).2)
            (((trivializationAt (TensorRSModel r s 𝕜 E)
                (fun x => TensorRSSpace r s I x) x₀) ⟨x, T x⟩).2)) x₀ := by
    exact ((contMDiffAt_const
      (c := modelApplyInputBilinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) r s)).clm_apply hθ).clm_apply hT
  refine hcombine.congr_of_eventuallyEq ?_
  filter_upwards
    [(trivializationAt E (TangentSpace I) x₀).open_baseSet.mem_nhds
      (mem_baseSet_trivializationAt E (TangentSpace I) x₀)] with x hx
  exact tensor0SModelAt_applyInput_eq (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (I := I)

01167772-943a-4c75-ab15-9f7b235777a8.explanation:
Under almost-everywhere strong measurability and integrable energy, equality of total area and energy is equivalent to orthogonality and equal norms almost everywhere.

The pointwise area-energy bound first supplies integrability of the area density by domination. For two integrable functions ordered almost everywhere, equal integrals are equivalent to equality almost everywhere. Applying the proved pointwise equality criterion therefore gives

$$A(v(x),w(x))=E(v(x),w(x))\ \text{a.e.}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle v(x),w(x)\rangle=0\ \text{and}\ \|v(x)\|=\|w(x)\|\ \text{a.e.}$$

0539c3a6-d718-4422-9183-3a398c35b441.explanation: Apply the manifold chain rule to f composed with p. The induced metric evaluates as the ambient metric on df of each tangent vector, so the two Gram matrices agree entrywise. Their determinants and square roots therefore agree.

0943befc-504f-4d6d-af2b-43ec35d7a1b3.explanation: This reduction retains one Open geometric child: constructing volume-controlled scalar and width profiles from a hypothetical counterexample. Given its data for each horizon, the proved trace constructor derives event finiteness from model radial comparison and the volume-loss budget, sorts the event times and restricts the profiles to a finite trace. Thus the Bishop-Gromov analytic prerequisites enter the existing width route through a proved nonaccumulation step. The geometric child, the parent and the Poincare goal remain Open; this is not a proof of Ricci-flow surgery or of the full geometric Bishop-Gromov theorem.

096644e2-0f01-45df-9752-41d89decd664.explanation:
For almost-everywhere strongly measurable fields with finite energy, we prove

$$\int_X A(v,w)\,d\mu\leq\int_X E(v,w)\,d\mu.$$

Cauchy-Schwarz and the identity

$$E(v,w)^2-A(v,w)^2=\frac{(\|v\|^2-\|w\|^2)^2}{4}+\langle v,w\rangle^2.$$

show that the area density lies between zero and the energy density at every point. The area density is a continuous function of the pair of vectors, hence is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Domination by the integrable energy density makes the area density integrable. Monotonicity of the integral gives the assertion.

0bbeaeb3-bf91-4538-ad63-f4a462576fdd.explanation: Reuse the specified metric to instantiate Mathlib's continuous Riemannian bundle and the induced extended metric with its compatible manifold topology. The set defining the ball is an extended-metric open ball, so Mathlib's openness theorem applies. The metric and distance definitions retain their original Mathlib/DifferentialGeometry provenance; this is OpenGA's interface corollary.

0fe76133-97aa-466f-b05d-8164a3b0a95c.explanation:
We prove that dyadic exhaustion upgrades the interval-wise form of Kleiner-Lott's Proposition 77.2 to all-time existence. Let $P$ be a Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff, $\mathrm{Def}(T)$ the predicate asserting that it is defined on all of $[0,T]$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Assume

$$\mathrm{Def}\big(2^{i}\varepsilon\big)\qquad\text{for every }i\in\mathbb N .$$

Then $\mathrm{Def}(T)$ holds for every $T\ge0$.

The proof idea is that the Archimedean property of the reals makes the dyadic times $2^i\varepsilon$ cofinal in $[0,\infty)$, and that being defined on $[0,T]$ is inherited by subintervals.

Let $T\ge0$. Since $\varepsilon>0$ and $2>1$, the powers of $2$ are unbounded, so there is $i\in\mathbb N$ with

$$\frac{T}{\varepsilon}<2^{i},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad T<2^{i}\varepsilon .$$

By hypothesis $\mathrm{Def}(2^{i}\varepsilon)$ holds, and the monotonicity field of the record, which records that a flow defined on $[0,T'']$ is defined on every $[0,S]$ with $0\le S\le T''$, yields $\mathrm{Def}(T)$.

The statement is the bridge between the way Proposition 77.2 is proved -- by induction over the blocks $[2^{j-1}\varepsilon,2^j\varepsilon]$, on which the parameters $r_j,\bar\delta_j,\kappa_j$ are constant -- and the unrestricted all-time statement used later in the argument.

140db3d0-6990-4dc7-85d7-5ebd389c8320.explanation:
At a point of a tangent-bundle chart base, the Gram matrix of a smooth Riemannian metric in the induced tangent basis is positive definite. Consequently its determinant is positive and it is invertible. The base-membership assumption ensures that the chart vectors form a basis.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

The proof uses the definitions and helper identities from the cited source. Its separate proved prerequisites are: The Gram quadratic form equals the metric norm square. The full source argument is retained, with its original hypotheses and source attribution.

15a12bda-4d91-481f-9492-2022ec9bf42b.explanation: The square of the area density is the two-by-two Gram determinant. Mathlib identifies the same determinant with the square of normDet. Expanding the Gram determinant and using symmetry of the real inner product gives equality of squares. Both quantities are nonnegative, hence they are equal. The area-density square and nonnegativity lemmas are retained as local helpers.

1ab970c0-c2d9-4f2b-8981-aa0e396e5db1.explanation:
On a compact Hausdorff smooth real manifold, let $g_t$ be a smooth Riemannian metric and $h$ a continuous real function. For the chosen subordinate smooth partition of unity $(\rho_\alpha)$ and chart measures $\mu_{\alpha,t}$, $$\sum_\alpha\int h\rho_\alpha\,d\mu_{\alpha,t}=\int h\,d\mu_{g_t}.$$ The finite sum runs over the active partition indices. This identifies the local derivative terms with the global volume integral.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

The proof uses the definitions and helper identities from the cited source. Its separate proved prerequisites are: Finite decomposition of continuous Riemannian integrals. The full source argument is retained, with its original hypotheses and source attribution.

215a8912-7522-41aa-b325-90cc2e896108.explanation:
For every real constant $c$ and time $t_0$, the function $f(t,x)=c$ satisfies `FunctionRegularAt` at $t_0$, with time derivative zero. This specializes the variation of weighted integrals to variation of total volume.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

A constant integrand is continuous and has zero time derivative. These identities supply every field of the regularity structure.

223f4a6c-2fec-4541-9065-86a7d3429698.explanation:
At a point of a tangent-bundle chart base, let $G(s)$ be the Gram matrix of a smooth Riemannian metric family. If its entries have derivatives given by the matrix $G'$ at $t$, then $$\frac{d}{dt}\sqrt{\det G(t)}=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(G(t)^{-1}G')\sqrt{\det G(t)}.$$ Positive definiteness comes from the metric and the chart base assumption.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

The proof uses the definitions and helper identities from the cited source. Its separate proved prerequisites are: Positive definiteness of metric Gram matrices on a chart base; Jacobi formula for the square root of a positive determinant. The full source argument is retained, with its original hypotheses and source attribution.

2283c781-4086-4880-9c6f-6556c635be55.explanation: Adjoin the endpoints 0 and T to the finite event set and enumerate the result in increasing order. An event strictly between adjacent partition points would have an index strictly between two consecutive natural numbers.

24400f2f-77a8-4a88-bd6a-c2dc9454b43d.explanation:
Let $f:\mathbb R^2\to E$ be $C^1$, $b_0,b_1$ an orthonormal basis, $P$ a measurable tangent lift, and $\Omega$ a parameter domain with finite area and finite Dirichlet energy. Then

$$\mathbf M(V_f)\le\frac12\int_\Omega\bigl(|df(b_0)|^2+|df(b_1)|^2\bigr)\,dx.$$

The Jacobian and tangent planes are those of the actual derivative. The proof reuses OpenGA's published integral area-energy comparison, which also enters the existing width-decay graph. This is CM equation (1.4) in a Euclidean parameter domain; no global frame on a sphere is asserted. The submitted proof preserves the reviewed OpenGA source; only imports and the solution binding are adapted.

255db963-969e-4e8a-abca-c84e122c509e.explanation:
Let $M$ be a compact Hausdorff smooth real manifold and $g_s$ a family of smooth Riemannian metrics satisfying `MetricFamilyRegularOn` on a neighborhood $U$ of $t$. Then $$\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{Vol}(M,g_t)=\frac12\int_M\operatorname{tr}_{g_t}\dot g_t\,d\mu_{g_t}.$$ The measure and volume are the constructed Riemannian ones. A smooth localization of time removes the need to assume regularity at all real times.

Choose a smooth time localization that agrees with the identity near the selected time and stays inside its regularity neighborhood. Apply global metric-family volume variation with constant integrand one, then use local equality of the original and localized volume functions.

25d76430-fc9b-4aaa-9490-50a596f993ff.explanation: Finite-extinction endgame with the exact existing topological goal. The geometric extracted-data construction supplies uniform width control; the proved deadline forces extinction, and finite surgery histories reconstruct standard connected-sum factors. The standard decomposition sketch uses the three explicit open topology lemmas and the proved sphere-covering base case. Four open leaves remain; this submission is a conditional reduction. https://github.com/MathNetwork/OpenGA/blob/20ce5fe376984e6628a05ab1622edd8dc64b3985/PoincareConjecture/Contributions/ExtinctionEndgame/Reduction.lean#L1-L75; Kleiner-Lott, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5, Section 3.2 and Lemmas 73.4, 81.2; Colding-Minicozzi, https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.0108, Theorem 1.7 and Corollary 1.11.

26ffe87c-abf2-41b7-874f-7f793cc78209.explanation:
For measurable $f:X\to E$, $P:X\to G_k(E)$ and $J:X\to[0,\infty)$ of finite integral, and every compactly supported continuous $\phi$ on positions and planes,

$$\int\phi\,d((f,P)_*(J\mu))=\int_X J(x)\phi(f(x),P(x))\,d\mu(x).$$ The submitted proof preserves the reviewed OpenGA source; only imports and the solution binding are adapted.

2e402417-5f76-4df8-a6d5-b9f1ff27d93b.explanation:
The cross-comparison hypothesis passes to integrals:

$$F(R)G(s)\le F(s)G(R).$$

Here $F$ and $G$ are the accumulated integrals of $f$ and $g$ over the intervals in the statement. Split the outer interval into the inner interval $A$ and the disjoint remainder $B$. Every $a\in A$ precedes every $b\in B$, so the hypothesis gives $f(b)g(a)\le f(a)g(b)$. Integrating this inequality first over $a$ and then over $b$ gives

$$\left(\int_B f\,d\mu\right)\left(\int_A g\,d\mu\right)\le\left(\int_A f\,d\mu\right)\left(\int_B g\,d\mu\right).$$

Add the common product of the two inner integrals and use additivity over the disjoint union. The proof works with extended nonnegative integrals, including infinite values.

Proof adapted from DifferentialGeometry v0.1.2, RatioIntegral.lean; the original argument and hypotheses are preserved.

31bc503a-b907-44ed-b41f-0b5a51dea75c.explanation:
Let $g_t$ satisfy `MetricFamilySmoothOn` on a time interval $D$, and let $f:N\to M$ be a fixed smooth immersion of a Hausdorff smooth surface. Then $$h_t=f^*g_t$$ satisfies `MetricFamilyRegularOn` on $D.regular$. The latter records the time derivatives and joint continuity of the induced chart Gram entries on that set. Compactness and a Ricci-flow equation are not needed for this step.

Express each induced Gram entry as the ambient metric evaluated on the differential of two surface chart vectors. Smoothness of the ambient family and the fixed immersion supplies its time derivative and joint continuity on the regular time set.

35352ec4-cb02-432f-9e67-b1254a2b5842.explanation:
At a point in the overlap of two tangent-bundle chart bases, the basis vectors satisfy $$e_i^{(1)}=\sum_k C_{ki}e_k^{(0)},$$ where $C$ is the transition matrix from the second basis to the first. This finite-dimensional basis identity is used to compare metric Gram matrices.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

The proof uses the definitions and helper identities from the cited source. The full source argument is retained, with its original hypotheses and source attribution.

3565c8c8-a1a0-47ca-b01c-17bdbcdf6e3d.explanation: Integrate the derivative upper bound on a common short interval using the mean-value inequality. The extra term given by the initial area gap divided by the interval length consumes at most that gap. The area-energy inequality bounds the initial slice supremum by the finite energy cap. Taking the supremum of the evolved slices gives exactly the short-time area comparison required by WidthComparisonData. The common interval and cutoff are essential hypotheses; pointwise variation of a single surface is insufficient.

379c6157-8439-4a05-93a5-f421e3a4e6ee.explanation:
Let $M$ be a compact Hausdorff smooth real manifold. Suppose $g_s$ satisfies `MetricFamilyRegularAt` and $f_s$ satisfies `FunctionRegularAt` at $t$. For a chosen partition function $\rho_\alpha$, $$\frac{d}{dt}\int f_t\rho_\alpha\,d\mu_{\alpha,t}=\int(\partial_t f_t+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_{g_t}\dot g_t\,f_t)\rho_\alpha\,d\mu_{\alpha,t}.$$ The proof derives the local domination and measurability requirements from these regularity and compactness assumptions.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

Pull the weighted chart integral back to the model space. Compact support of the partition function and joint regularity give an integrable local derivative bound. Differentiate under the integral and return to the chart measure.

4182e183-83c4-4680-a218-28f8530af82f.explanation:
Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on a Hausdorff smooth manifold and let $\rho$ be a smooth partition of unity subordinate to the atlas. For every compact set $K$, $$\mu_{g,\rho}(K)<\infty.$$ The proof uses local finiteness of the partition and chart-local finiteness. Compactness of the entire manifold is not assumed.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

The proof uses the definitions and helper identities from the cited source. Its separate proved prerequisites are: Finiteness of a chart measure on compact subsets of its source. The full source argument is retained, with its original hypotheses and source attribution.

42885aae-9f1a-4edc-b4c4-d8e3820e630a.explanation:
Assume the open comparison-data construction target. It supplies one initial width bound valid for every finite horizon and a trace of scalar and width profiles on each such horizon. Keep its partition, profiles, initial bounds, continuity and jump inequalities.

At each interior time the proved area-energy comparison theorem gives an eventual upper bound on the right-hand difference quotients of the width. The real right-neighborhood filter is nontrivial, so an eventual bound implies the frequently occurring bound required by ScalarWidthTrace. This fills its remaining width slope field.

The conclusion remains conditional on constructing the geometric comparison data; neither this reduction nor the analytic comparison theorem proves the Poincare conjecture independently.

471ac235-7f0c-425b-baeb-5ddc5195c1b5.explanation:
Let $g_s$ satisfy `MetricFamilyRegularAt`, including joint continuity of its chart Gram entries and their time derivatives on each entire chart-time domain. If $G_\alpha(s,x)$ is its Gram matrix in chart $\alpha$, then $$(s,x)\longmapsto\operatorname{tr}(G_\alpha(s,x)^{-1}\partial_sG_\alpha(s,x))$$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ times the chart base. This supplies the local continuity used in differentiating volume.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

The proof uses the definitions and helper identities from the cited source. Its separate proved prerequisites are: Positive definiteness of metric Gram matrices on a chart base. The full source argument is retained, with its original hypotheses and source attribution.

4995da0a-eb7c-43ad-9c8a-4e4576888aef.explanation:

6d178906-6119-48c0-b672-0f3881b70643.explanation:
Let $0=t_0<\cdots<t_n$ be the given finite partition and let $r_i$ be the continuous profiles. We prove
$$r_i(t)\ge -\frac{6}{1+4t}\qquad(t_i\le t\le t_{i+1})$$
under the lower right Dini inequality, the initial lower bound, and the upward-jump inequalities in the statement.

First consider one interval $[a,b]$ with $a\ge0$ and a continuous profile $r$ whose initial value is at least $-6/(1+4a)$. For $\varepsilon>0$, use the lower comparison function
$$b_\varepsilon(t)=-\frac{6}{1+4t}-\varepsilon.$$
The denominator is positive. Writing $A=6/(1+4t)>0$, its derivative satisfies
$$\frac23 b_\varepsilon(t)^2-b_\varepsilon'(t)
=\frac43 A\varepsilon+\frac23\varepsilon^2>0.$$
Thus, at a contact point, the assumed lower right Dini derivative of $r$ is strictly larger than the derivative of $b_\varepsilon$. The one-dimensional comparison principle, applied to the negative profile, gives $r\ge b_\varepsilon$ on the closed interval. The hypothesis on eventual slopes supplies the required frequent slope estimates for the negative profile. Letting $\varepsilon$ decrease to zero gives $r(t)\ge-6/(1+4t)$, including the right endpoint.

For the first interval, $t_0=0$ and $r_0(0)\ge-6$ supply the initial comparison. Suppose the bound holds on interval $i$. At its right endpoint, the jump condition gives
$$r_{i+1}(t_{i+1})\ge r_i(t_{i+1})\ge-\frac6{1+4t_{i+1}}.$$
This starts the same comparison on interval $i+1$. Induction proves the claim on every interval. In particular, both one-sided profile values at each joining time satisfy the bound.

The analytic comparison is the step used in [Kleiner-Lott, proof of Lemma 79.11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=154), with the scalar differential inequality from Appendix B. Its geometric application requires separately verifying the profile hypotheses for a Ricci flow.

Dividing by $s-t>0$ proves the eventual slope estimate. The choice of $j$ may depend on $s$; the neighborhood is uniform because the comparison estimate holds for every sufficiently large index.

98612d40-bcb7-4333-afa7-69b60e20dfdc.explanation:
This is a conditional reduction of the three-dimensional topological Poincaré theorem, not a complete proof. Its unproved geometric input is `PoincareFormalization.spherical_cover_of_finite_fundamental_group`:
$$\text{a closed connected 3-manifold with finite fundamental group admits a covering }S^3\to M.$$
That input is a topological consequence of elliptization; see Morgan–Tian, *Ricci Flow and the Poincaré Conjecture* (2007), Corollary 0.2(b), p. x, and footnote 1, p. ix, https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Ricci-pdf.pdf. The geometric input remains open in Lean.

For the mission's simply connected manifold $M$, the fundamental group at any chosen point is trivial and hence finite. Applying the geometric input gives a covering
$$p:S^3\longrightarrow M.$$
The sphere is connected by Mathlib's connectedness theorem for spheres in real vector spaces of dimension greater than one. The manifold is locally path connected because its charts take values in Euclidean 3-space. The independently proved covering-space lemma `PoincareFormalization.covering_is_homeomorph` therefore makes $p$ a homeomorphism. Its inverse has the exact type required by the mission.

No Ricci-flow existence, singularity control, surgery, or extinction theorem is proved by this reduction. Those substantive geometric obligations remain inside the open elliptization input. The root must remain open until that input is proved.

The two terms on the right are nonnegative. Equality of the densities forces both to vanish. Conversely, orthogonality and equal norms make the right-hand side zero; nonnegativity of both densities then gives equality.

bbe6fec0-1a12-4eba-bb85-2c00ebf62342.explanation:
Let $p:E\to X$ be a covering map, with $E$ nonempty and connected and $X$ simply connected and locally path connected. Then $p$ is a homeomorphism.

Choose $e_0\in E$. The lifting criterion gives a continuous lift $s:X\to E$ of the identity with
$$p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad s(p(e_0))=e_0.$$
The maps $s\circ p$ and $\operatorname{id}_E$ lift the same map and agree at $e_0$. Uniqueness of lifts on the connected space $E$ gives
$$s\circ p=\operatorname{id}_E.$$
Thus $p$ has a continuous inverse.

This is a corollary of Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §1.3, Propositions 1.33–1.34, pp. 61–62, https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf. The formal proof uses Mathlib's existing lifting and lift-uniqueness theorems. It imports no platform theorem.

be7d0fdd-7cd7-42df-b7a2-98b351f35160.explanation:
We construct the parameter functions of a Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff from the dyadic sequences of constants produced by Kleiner-Lott's Proposition 77.2. Given $\varepsilon>0$ and nonincreasing sequences of positive reals $(r_j)_{j\ge0}$, $(\delta_j)_{j\ge0}$, we produce positive nonincreasing $r,\delta:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ with

$$r(t)=r_j,\qquad \delta(t)=\delta_j\qquad (2^{j}\varepsilon\le t<2^{j+1}\varepsilon),$$

and $r(t)=r_0$, $\delta(t)=\delta_0$ on $[0,\varepsilon)$.

The proof idea is to define the block index of a time directly as an infimum rather than through a logarithm: for $t\in\mathbb R$ put

$$\iota(t)=\min\{j\in\mathbb N:\ t<2^{j+1}\varepsilon\},$$

and set $r(t)=r_{\iota(t)}$, $\delta(t)=\delta_{\iota(t)}$. Three facts about $\iota$ are needed.

First, $\iota$ is well defined: the set is nonempty because the powers of $2$ are unbounded, so $t/\varepsilon<2^{j}$ for some $j$, and hence $t<2^{j+1}\varepsilon$. Consequently $t<2^{\iota(t)+1}\varepsilon$ always holds.

Second, $\iota$ is monotone: if $t\le t'$ then $t<2^{\iota(t')+1}\varepsilon$, so $\iota(t')$ belongs to the set defining $\iota(t)$, whence $\iota(t)\le\iota(t')$. Since the sequences are nonincreasing, $r$ and $\delta$ are nonincreasing on the whole line, in particular on $[0,\infty)$

cb01e3bc-e1ec-491a-b7e3-6a04684c2a09.explanation:
For a family $g_s$ satisfying `MetricFamilyRegularAt` and a fixed time $t$, $$x\longmapsto\operatorname{tr}_{g_t}\dot g_t(x)$$ is continuous on the smooth manifold. The trace is the chart-independent quantity defined from the Gram matrix. This lets compactness provide the bounds needed for integration.

cf1e62af-8072-4890-9001-f53199622fc5.explanation:
Let $A$ be a set in a finite-dimensional real normed model space with its chosen Haar measure. Suppose $F(t,\cdot)$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable near $t_0$, $F(t_0,\cdot)$ is integrable, the proposed derivative $F'(t_0,\cdot)$ is measurable, and $|F'(t,y)|\le b(y)$ almost everywhere for all $t$ in a neighborhood of $t_0$, with $b$ integrable. If $\partial_tF=F'$ there, then $$\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=t_0}\int_A F(t,y)\,dy=\int_A F'(t_0,y)\,dy,$$ and the derivative integrand is integrable.

Apply dominated differentiation to model Haar measure restricted to the target set, retaining the stated measurability, integrability, neighborhood and pointwise derivative assumptions.

d543d39b-4273-4b91-826f-1b9c8c6191ee.explanation:
This is a conditional reduction of the topological Poincare conjecture to the geometric profile-extraction theorem. That child remains open. The two analytic inputs, scalar comparison and the width deadline, are proved independently.

Suppose a compact simply connected Hausdorff topological three-manifold $M$ were not homeomorphic to $S^3$. The open geometric child supplies a number $W_0$, fixed before the final time, and finite scalar-width traces on arbitrarily long intervals. The scalar comparison theorem gives
$$r_i(t)\ge-\frac6{1+4t}.$$
Because every width is nonnegative, the coupled width inequality implies
$$D_+w_i(t)\le-4\pi-\frac12r_i(t)w_i(t)\le-4\pi+\frac3{1+4t}w_i(t).$$
This is precisely the width-deadline inequality with $C=1/4$. The downward jump hypothesis permits the deadline theorem to apply across all pieces, giving
$$T\le T_*:=\left((1/4)^{1/4}+\frac{W_0}{16\pi(1/4)^{3/4}}\right)^4-\frac14.$$
Choose $T=\max(T_*,0)+1$. The geometric child supplies a trace at this positive time, while the analytic bound rules it out. This contradiction gives the required homeomorphism.

The unresolved geometric child includes smoothing, surgery existence, survival/topology, and the production of compatible scalar and width profiles. The reduction does not prove those ingredients or any of the four large geometric milestones. Every imported theorem is used in the argument; no extra import is present solely to create a graph edge.

d9b236c0-582f-4d62-9153-94a726e86857.explanation:
For real square matrices $A,B$ on a finite index type, $$\sum_\sigma\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\sum_k B_{\sigma(k),k}\prod_{i\ne k}A_{\sigma(i),i}=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(A)B).$$ This algebraic identity is valid even when $A$ is singular and connects the determinant expansion to Jacobi's formula.

Proof from DifferentialGeometry, preserved and packaged by OpenGA with source attribution.

Expand the adjugate using cofactors and the trace using its diagonal sum, then reindex the finite sums to match the differentiated determinant expansion.

e04116f7-6882-4385-adb2-3d369736d0a3.explanation: Apply the proved normalized radial integral comparison from the removal radius to the reference radius. Combine the anchor lower bound with containment in the removed material, then clear the positive finite model-volume denominator. This is a conditional analytic consequence; geometric containment and the anchor are inputs.

e226c921-de2b-4b97-bc82-2365ef39853d.explanation:
The cross-comparison hypothesis passes to integrals:

$$F(R)G(s)\le F(s)G(R).$$

Here $F$ and $G$ are the accumulated integrals of $f$ and $g$ over the intervals in the statement. Split the outer interval into the inner interval $A$ and the disjoint remainder $B$. Every $a\in A$ precedes every $b\in B$, so the hypothesis gives $f(b)g(a)\le f(a)g(b)$. Integrating this inequality first over $a$ and then over $b$ gives

$$\left(\int_B f\,d\mu\right)\left(\int_A g\,d\mu\right)\le\left(\int_A f\,d\mu\right)\left(\int_B g\,d\mu\right).$$

Add the common product of the two inner integrals and use additivity over the disjoint union. The proof works with extended nonnegative integrals, including infinite values.

Proof adapted from DifferentialGeometry v0.1.2, RatioIntegral.lean; the original argument and hypotheses are preserved.

e2b775eb-e5c4-401a-be7c-8c5011d97752.explanation: Reduce the unchanged process-existence statement to the Open measured-data construction. e6e79781-a2e6-46ea-97e2-2db7537f9abb.explanation: Use the proved pointwise equality of area densities at every point of the measurable parameter domain. The set-integral congruence theorem then identifies the two Bochner integrals. The density result is the actual imported proof dependency.

e793e526-170e-4323-a690-5dcb62c9a900.explanation:
On a compact Hausdorff smooth manifold with the stated sigma-compactness instance, for any continuous real function $h$ and smooth Riemannian metric $g$, $$\int h\,d\mu_g=\sum_{\alpha\in F}\int h\,d(\rho_\alpha\mu_{\alpha,g}).$$ The measures and active finite partition are those of the chosen atlas. This converts global integration into finitely many chart integrals.

ea395ce5-9ba3-4bfe-b7e6-bb18563f2f6f.explanation: Use geodesic-ball openness and the proved positive-measure theorem. Finiteness makes the real conversion positive; division by the positive normalization preserves positivity.

ecffef77-6ae4-4288-95a2-b62ceb5e9571.explanation: Let $f$, $P$, $Q$ and $J\ge0$ be measurable, with finite integral of $J$. If $P(x)=Q(x)$ for almost every $x$ with $J(x)\ne0$, then $(f,P)_*(J\mu)=(f,Q)_*(J\mu)$. Thus arbitrary tangent-plane choices on the zero-density set have no effect. The submitted proof preserves the reviewed OpenGA source; only imports and the solution binding are adapted.

f0552af4-769d-4fe4-8754-b9e01fd5718b.explanation:
The conclusion is the explicit upper bound
$$t_n\le\left(C^{1/4}+\frac{W_0}{16\pi C^{3/4}}\right)^4-C.$$
For $\varepsilon>0$, compare every width segment with the same solution $B_\varepsilon$ of
$$B_\varepsilon'=\frac{3}{4(t+C)}B_\varepsilon-4\pi+\varepsilon,\qquad B_\varepsilon(0)=W_0+\varepsilon.$$
Its explicit expression is
$$B_\varepsilon(t)=\frac{W_0+\varepsilon}{C^{3/4}}(t+C)^{3/4}+4(\varepsilon-4\pi)\big((t+C)-C^{1/4}(t+C)^{3/4}\big).$$
At a contact point the assumed lower-Dini upper bound is strictly below the derivative of this comparison function. The one-sided comparison lemma therefore bounds the width on each interval. A downward jump preserves the endpoint inequality, so induction carries the same comparison through all intervals without changing the initial constant.

Continuity in $\varepsilon$ gives $w_{n-1}(t_n)\le B_0(t_n)$. Since the final width is nonnegative and $(t_n+C)^{3/4}>0$, factoring this expression yields
$$16\pi\big((t_n+C)^{1/4}-C^{1/4}\big)\le\frac{W_0}{C^{3/4}}.$$
Dividing by $16\pi$ and taking fourth powers proves the bound. The proof uses only Mathlib and contains no unproved geometric inputs.

f1a903ae-f375-4652-a2b3-1e916e38d315.explanation:
We prove all-time existence for a Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff, in the form

$$\mathrm{Def}(T)\qquad\text{for every }T\ge 0,$$

where $\mathrm{Def}(T)$ is the predicate of the record $P$ asserting that the flow with cutoff, started from the given normalized initial condition, is defined on the whole interval $[0,T]$, empty time slices being allowed.

The hypotheses used are exactly the fields of the record: $\mathrm{Def}(0)$

f344bf48-e3ea-49fa-b041-ee5232abefba.explanation:
Let $g_s$ satisfy `MetricFamilyRegularAt`. At a point in the overlap of two chart bases, let $C$ be the time-independent transition matrix of their tangent bases and $G_0,G_1$ the metric Gram matrices. Then $$\dot G_1(t)=C^{T}\dot G_0(t)C.$$ This transfers the metric time derivative between charts.

f7b7217a-bf10-417c-8b1c-0abe47d70e42.explanation: If Euclidean varifolds $V_i$ converge weakly to $V$, then for every continuous compactly supported spatial function $\phi$, $\int\phi\,d\|V_i\|\to\int\phi\,d\|V\|$. f7eb9e91-abc0-4836-98f5-12e6d9739018.explanation:

f82f6ab1-1244-450b-b0f9-947f5d6009dd.explanation: Keep the existing measured-surgery existence statement unchanged. fa5f156d-d3f8-45b0-8007-1c1454024b80.explanation:
Let $G$ be the chart Gram matrix of a smooth metric $g$, and let $c_i$ be real coefficients. For the chart-induced vectors $e_i$, $$c^TGc=g\left(\sum_i c_ie_i,\sum_j c_je_j\right).$$ This bilinear identity holds with the chart-vector definitions used in the formal statement and proves positivity on the chart base.

fb426a2c-720c-423b-ac15-0e0405f96116.explanation:
Suppose every chart Gram entry $G_{ij}(t,x)$ of a smooth metric family has a time derivative $D_{ij}(t,x)$ for every real time on its chart base, and both $G_{ij}$ and $D_{ij}$ are jointly continuous there. Then the family satisfies `MetricFamilyRegularAt` at every specified time. This packages exactly those global chart-time hypotheses; it does not assert their existence for arbitrary metric families.

fd6f90da-3fa3-48c4-95a0-f36e42b9fe72.explanation: Continuity and positivity of the model density give a positive finite model integral at every positive radius.
